conceptZh: 雙腳大步跨開的珊瑚紅木質工藝腿，一腳向左下劃出主筆，另一腳向右下靠緊撐住，展現互相依靠站立成「人」字的意象。
object: A pair of sleek coral-red wooden craft legs on a clean cream-colored backdrop.
morph: The left leg sweeps diagonally down-left to form the left stroke (撇), while the right leg leans against its top upper side and extends down-right (捺), forming the balanced structure of '人'.
creativeAngle: 不同於舊版公仔收縮頭手的做法，改以兩條大步踩踏的木質工藝腿。透過「一腳開步、一腳靠緊支撐」的物理動態，生動呈現「人」字筆劃互相依靠與獨立站立的意象。
promptEn:
An 8-second, 4K resolution educational animation for children aged 6-8 teaching the Traditional Chinese character '人' (person).

0:00-0:02: On a clean, bright cream studio background, two sleek, polished coral-red wooden craft legs stand centered. A warm Taiwanese Mandarin voiceover clearly pronounces the target character ㄖㄣˊ (rén).

0:02-0:05: The left wooden leg smoothly sweeps down and to the left, carving out a bold diagonal stroke (撇). Immediately after, the right leg tilts over, rests its top edge against the upper portion of the left stroke, and extends diagonally down to the right (捺) to form a wide, balanced stance. The wooden textures seamlessly smooth out into a single, clean, saturated coral-red Traditional Chinese glyph '人'. The voiceover pronounces ㄖㄣˊ (rén) again.

0:05-0:08: The completed glyph '人' rests perfectly motionless in the center of the frame, filling approximately 70% of the frame height with generous background margins. The solid coral-red strokes stand out with rich contrast against the soft cream lighting. The voiceover clearly repeats ㄖㄣˊ (rén) two final times for memory retention.

Shot with a fixed centered studio camera, soft fill lighting, no camera motion, no text overlays, no watermarks, no flashes, and zero background clutter.

conceptZh: 自以為隱形的布忍者躲進「人」字兩筆之間，卻整隻露出來；擠到筆畫後方又露出頭腳，最後側身才成功藏好。
object: One rigid coral-red cutout of 人 and an original tiny felt ninja with a plump, squashable body.
morph: The correctly formed glyph stays rigid throughout. Its open space exposes the ninja's failed hiding attempt; the broad upper portion of its left-falling stroke finally conceals his sideways felt silhouette.
creativeAngle: 改用完整字形當躲藏道具，不再把身體變成筆畫。忍者誤把兩筆間的空隙當掩護，再把自己擠得頭腳外露，讓「藏不好」的笑點凸顯字形的實心筆畫與留白。
promptEn:
Create an 8-second stylized stop-motion-style animation with tactile felt and matte painted wood. Use a fixed frontal camera and a bright, warm cream studio background. Center one saturated coral-red wooden cutout of the Traditional Chinese glyph 人, correctly formed with a left-falling 撇 and a right-falling 捺 joining below the top of the first stroke. It fills approximately 70% of frame height, with generous margins and both stroke tips fully visible. Preserve this exact rigid silhouette throughout.

The sole animated lead is an original tiny felt ninja with visible stitching, a plum-colored fabric hood, expressive embroidered eyes and a plump, compressible body. His personality is absolute confidence in his spectacularly poor hiding skills. The glyph is the only supporting object.

From 0.0–1.5 seconds, the ninja tiptoes into the open space between the two strokes, freezes in a dramatic stealth crouch and smugly closes his eyes. His entire body remains plainly visible through the gap. Allow a brief pause for the mistake to register. From 1.5–3.6 seconds, he opens one eye, looks up at the empty space above him and hastily scoots behind the broad upper portion of the left-falling stroke. He squeezes himself down to hide, but his soft body spreads sideways: his hood pops out on one edge and both padded feet pop out on the opposite edge. Hold this absurd peekaboo silhouette for a short beat; the wooden stroke never bends or changes. From 3.6–4.6 seconds, he notices his exposed feet, releases the squeeze and pivots edge-on behind the same stroke. His thin felt profile finally disappears completely. Use depth staging so the glyph remains the central teaching subject and the hiding action reads clearly.

From 4.6–8.0 seconds, hold the finished glyph completely still and unobstructed, with the ninja fully concealed. Only the single glyph 人 appears as on-screen text.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly: 「人、人、家人」. Say the first 人 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 家人 around 5.3 seconds during the clear final hold. Use the usual ㄖㄣˊ pronunciation for 人. Stop speaking after the word. Add only soft felt shuffles and a gentle comic fabric squeak beneath the voice; no music. Keep the vocabulary audio-only, with no subtitles, other text, logos, watermarks, clutter or flashing effects.
